source_notes: The inspected source is arXiv:2201.01036v1, stamped 4 January 2022. Its title and authors match the corpus entry. The census is explicitly version-specific and does not assert equality with the later 2024 publication.
The PDF and its hash are retained in the external source cache; repository evidence contains only main-text extracts, inspected images, provenance and the appendix-heading crop.
Nonzero coefficient groups exclude the zero class. Group count and support size are distinct, and the feasible problem gives upper bounds rather than exact counts.
Grouping sensitivity measures prediction separation per grouping discrepancy. The grouping distance is defined by injections and is not silently symmetrized.
The minimax ratio r is defined within Theorem 2.5. The post-theorem restricted-eigenvalue conjecture is not imposed as a hypothesis.
Algorithm 2 uses a general convex lower-bounded objective and set-valued projection. Theorem 3.2 concerns its infinite sequence and limit c, not convergence to a specified global minimizer.

Potential nonunique or unattained minima, oracle group-collapse discrepancies, arbitrary initialization, stopping-rule conventions and denominator edge cases are retained as explicit unresolved source details.
Screening, CoSaMP, MIO formulations and proof-only stationary-point results are not counted as prerequisites of these theorem statements.

unresolved_source_references.text: The source specifies a scalar Gaussian error law and iid observations but does not explicitly state independence of the error from the covariates in this passage. No conditional-error or design assumption is inserted.

The set-builder lists gamma in R^K without writing an existential quantifier. The source constraint is retained; the auxiliary gamma is understood as a feasibility witness, without requiring K distinct occupied groups.

The minima and least-squares solutions are printed without attainment or uniqueness assumptions. The group-equality oracle constraint and the subsequent unrestricted collapsed-design regression need not define the same set if fitted groups merge or vanish. Both source formulations are retained without adding design-rank or nonzero-coefficient conditions.

The balanced subclass uses group labels indexed by K0 although Theta(K0,s0) is an upper-bound class; no exact-group-count restriction is inserted. The ratio r can have a zero or undefined denominator, and the displayed parameter range permits floor((K0+3)/4)*p=1, making the logarithmic denominator zero. No extra positivity, cardinality or empty-class convention is supplied.

The Lipschitz-gradient condition is stated for points in Theta(K,s), but Algorithm 2 initializes theta1 anywhere in R^(p+q). The source does not explicitly require a feasible initialization; no such requirement is added.

The algorithm prints a stopping tolerance, while Theorem 3.2 concerns its infinite update sequence and every positive integer M. The source does not state an extension after termination. The finite algorithm and infinite-sequence theorem are preserved separately.

ambient_resolution: The parameter theta concatenates beta in R^p and nuisance alpha in R^q. The existence of a gamma vector supplies at most K distinct nonzero beta values; repeated or zero gamma entries are not ruled out by the feasible-set definition.
The grouping operator excludes zero coefficients, while its index operator includes the zero class when evaluated at r=0. Group counts and support sizes have distinct meanings.

The distance of Definition 2.1 uses injections from the smaller nonzero grouping into the larger one. Its asymmetric definition is valid for the candidate-vs-truth comparison in c_min because the feasible class bounds candidate group count by the true count.

The statistical probability statements use the regression model and iid observation convention. The deterministic grouping sensitivity, parameter class and projection definitions do not themselves require Gaussian sampling.

Theorem 2.5 defines r(X,Z,K0,s0) inside its own statement. No extra API is invented for that local binder. Its estimator infimum ranges over arbitrary estimators of the grouping under the stated sampling model.

Theorem 3.2 uses a general convex, lower-bounded objective with Lipschitz gradient as specified in Section 3.2. It does not require the squared-error objective, Gaussian errors, a true grouping, or the statistical parameter subclasses.
The squared Euclidean projection is set-valued. Algorithm 2 selects an element at each step; the theorem does not specify a unique projection or a particular implementation.
Theorem 3.2 supplies the limiting real constant c with g(theta_m) decreasing to c. It is not defined as the global minimum or the lower-bound constant C2.
review_limits: The audit checks source statement fidelity and dependencies rather than certifying the proofs or repairing unstated conventions.
